method: manual web verification against rank 2-3 authorities; no bank records modified

records.keyClaim: Homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing is least expected in frontal lesion (occipital sign).

citations.quote: Lesions that affect the occipital lobe will result in contralateral hemianopia with macular sparing

records.reviewerNote: Frontal features (primitive reflexes, leg weakness, incontinence, executive loss) all typical.

records.keyClaim: Pituitary adenoma most likely cause of bitemporal hemianopia among options.

citations.quote: commonly results from a tumor or lesion impinging on the optic chiasm

records.reviewerNote: Chiasm lies superior to pituitary (same source).

records.keyClaim: Basilar terminates as posterior cerebral arteries.

citations.quote: the basilar artery bifurcates into its 2 terminal branches, the posterior cerebral arteries

records.keyClaim: Extracranial optic nerve supplied by ophthalmic artery.

citations.quote: optic nerve is supplied by the internal carotid artery, specifically the superior hypophyseal and ophthalmic arteries

records.reviewerNote: Identical stem to p1586-q0058: possible duplicate record, flag for bank dedup.

nigrostriatal pathway ... critically involved in the motor deficits observed in Parkinson disease

records.keyClaim: Two-point discrimination loss is parietal, least expected in frontal lesion.

citations.quote: contains the primary somatosensory cortex ... touch, pressure, temperature, and pain

citations.quote: from the lateral ventricle to the third ventricle via the foramen of Monro, from third to the fourth ventricle via the cerebral aqueduct

records.reviewerNote: Options A/B/C/E all true (130-150mL; lateral-dominant production; temporal horn; 4th ventricle in brainstem).

citations.quote: Dorsal fibers ... travel through the posterior temporal lobe and the parietal lobe ... transmit ... inferior visual field

citations.quote: lateral spinothalamic tract carries information about pain and temperature

citations.quote: ACAs supply all of the medial surfaces of the frontal and parietal lobe ... primary motor, primary sensory cortices

citations.quote: C7 | Triceps & Wrist flexion | Index/Middle/Ring Paresthesia | Triceps

records.keyClaim: Diplopia on reading/downstairs implicates trochlear (superior oblique).

citations.quote: difficulty looking downwards ... reading a book ... descending stairs

records.keyClaim: Absent consensual blink with intact direct = efferent (facial) lesion on the unresponsive side.

citations.quote: Afferent input from the ophthalmic division ... stimulate the orbicularis oculi muscles bilaterally

records.reviewerNote: Direct left intact proves left afferent + left efferent work; absent right consensual isolates right VII.

records.keyClaim: Pupil-sparing CN III palsy is typically diabetic microvascular.

citations.quote: Microvascular ischemia ... is the most common etiology in adults ... ischemic injury typically sparing parasympathetic fibers
Diabetic third nerve palsy ... pupil-sparing ... microvascular infarction

records.reviewerNote: Aneurysmal compression typically dilates the pupil.

records.keyClaim: Glossopharyngeal palsy abolishes the gag reflex (afferent limb).

citations.quote: If the glossopharyngeal (IX) nerve is damaged ... there is no response when touched

records.reviewerNote: Tongue fasciculations = XII; uvular deviation = X; jaw jerk = V; hoarseness = X.

records.keyClaim: Glossopharyngeal is the gag afferent; vagus the efferent.

citations.quote: glossopharyngeal (CN IX) and vagus (CN X) nerves, which serve as the afferent (sensory) and the efferent (motor) limbs

records.keyClaim: Cerebellopontine-angle tumours most often involve VIII (acoustic neuroma).

citations.quote: commonly located in the cerebellopontine angle, near the cochlear and vestibular nerves

records.reviewerNote: Vestibular schwannoma = 75-85% of CPA tumours (CPA Cancer, NBK559116).

records.keyClaim: Abducens palsy leaves medial rectus unopposed causing convergent squint.

citations.quote: innervate the lateral rectus muscle, which then abducts the eye
down-and-out eye position due to the unopposed action of the lateral rectus ... and superior oblique

records.reviewerNote: A/B/C/D all false (SO=IV; horizontal not vertical diplopia; nucleus in pons; enters via superior orbital fissure).

records.keyClaim: Internal auditory meatus contains VII and VIII.

citations.quote: commonly involve the cerebellopontine angle (CPA), the internal auditory canal (IAC), or the inner ear
grows between the vestibulocochlear nerve and the facial nerve inside the inner ear canal

records.keyClaim: Depressed-abducted eye with ptosis = CN III palsy (unopposed LR + SO).

citations.quote: characteristic down-and-out eye position ... Ptosis occurs due to paralysis of the levator palpebrae superioris

records.keyClaim: Trochlear nerve innervates superior oblique only.

citations.quote: The only muscle the trochlear nerve innervates, the superior oblique muscle

records.keyClaim: Spinal accessory innervates SCM and trapezius.

citations.quote: innervates the sternocleidomastoid (SCM) and trapezius muscles through its spinal root

records.keyClaim: Facial nerve divides into five terminal branches within the parotid.

citations.quote: enters the parotid gland ... five branches emerge
Within the parotid gland, the facial nerve divides into five branches: Temporal, Zygomatic, Buccal, Marginal mandibular, Cervical

records.keyClaim: Glossopharyngeal is NOT the gag efferent (vagus is); all other statements true.

citations.quote: afferent (sensory) and the efferent (motor) limbs ... CN IX ... CN X
supply motor innervation to the stylopharyngeus muscle ... parasympathetic innervation to the parotid glands

records.keyClaim: Bank key says abducens, but the stem references an image unavailable to this audit.

records.keyClaim: Facial nerve traverses the internal acoustic meatus.

citations.quote: pass through the posterior cranial fossa along with the vestibulocochlear nerve ... entering the internal acoustic meatus

records.reviewerNote: It exits the skull via the stylomastoid foramen; IAM is its transit, matching key D among options.

records.keyClaim: Masseter wasting + jaw-opening weakness + anterior-tongue numbness = mandibular nerve (V3).

citations.quote: mandibular nerve ... carries both afferent and efferent fibers ... muscles of mastication ... anterior two-thirds of the tongue

records.keyClaim: Mandibular nerve does NOT innervate orbicularis oculi (facial nerve does).

citations.quote: motor muscular branches to the medial pterygoid, tensor tympani, and tensor veli palatini ... mastication muscles

records.reviewerNote: A/B/C/E all true (infratemporal course, foramen ovale, anterior tongue sensory, mixed nerve).

records.keyClaim: Oculomotor nerve runs in the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus.

citations.quote: enters the cavernous sinus, where it runs on the roof and lateral wall

records.reviewerNote: A/B/C/E false (mixed? no - pure motor + parasymp; not all EOMs; constricts pupil; enters via superior orbital fissure).

records.keyClaim: Uvula deviates away from a vagal lesion, so rightward deviation implicates the left vagus.

citations.quote: uvula deviation (towards the opposite side of the lesion)

records.keyClaim: Mandibular division spares the upper lip (maxillary territory).

citations.quote: maxillary branch ... upper lip ... mandibular branch ... external ear, chin, lower lip, anterior two-thirds of the tongue

records.keyClaim: Vagus carries visceral afferents from aortic arch baroreceptors.

citations.quote: inferior ganglion of X provides afferent general visceral fibers to the carotid and aortic bodies

records.reviewerNote: A/B/D/E false (foramen ovale=V3; oropharynx general sensation=V; parotid=IX; gag afferent=IX).

records.keyClaim: Maxillary division spares the external ear (mandibular territory).

citations.quote: maxillary branch ... superior palate, upper lip, upper molar ... nasal cavity ... lower eyelid

records.reviewerNote: External ear supplied via mandibular (auriculotemporal).

records.keyClaim: Hyperacusis (stapedius dysfunction) occurs in facial palsy.

citations.quote: hyperacusis ... due the stapedius muscle ... being affected

records.reviewerNote: Ptosis/ophthalmoplegia are oculomotor; facial sensory loss is trigeminal.

records.keyClaim: Lingual nerve carries touch (not taste) from anterior tongue; chorda tympani carries taste/salivation.

citations.quote: innervates the mucous membrane of the anterior two-thirds ... chorda tympani ... responsible for taste perception ... and secretory/motor innervation of glands

records.reviewerNote: Taste + salivation intact isolates the lingual (general sensory) division.

records.keyClaim: Inability to raise the eyelid (levator/CN III) is NOT a facial palsy feature; lagophthalmos is.

citations.quote: Ptosis occurs due to paralysis of the levator palpebrae superioris muscle

records.reviewerNote: A-D (hyperacusis, reduced salivation/lacrimation, taste loss) are all VII features.

records.keyClaim: Tongue deviation toward the lesion is hypoglossal (XII), not vagal.

citations.quote: the tongue, when protruded, deviates towards the damaged nerve

records.reviewerNote: A/C/D/E (uvula away, hoarseness, gag loss, dysphagia) are vagal.

records.keyClaim: Glossopharyngeal provides parotid parasympathetics.

citations.quote: provide parasympathetic innervation to the parotid glands

records.reviewerNote: A-D false (efferent=vagus; exits via jugular foramen; taste post-third; tensor veli palatini=V3).
